findings.description: This condition discards `response.modelId` whenever its bare value equals the requested model. On the default native OpenAI stream path, the pinned AI SDK sets response metadata's `modelId` from the provider's `response.created.response.model`, so the normal successful `gpt-5.6-sol` response is real provider evidence, not a configured fallback; the emitted generation nevertheless has `modelReported: null` (confirmed by executing that path). Distinguish the Claude configured fallback from provider-sourced response metadata instead of using equality, and retain the OpenAI identity.
findings.failureMode: A normal native OpenAI judge response reports exactly the requested model; decision provenance and ensemble output incorrectly report the served model as unknown.
findings.title: Keep equal provider-reported model identities

findings.description: On the default native judge route, a successful `generateAdjudication` is returned here, but that pending return is overridden if `FactoryCredentialStore.close()` rejects in the following `finally`. `judgePath` then receives only a plain cleanup error, so `runEnsemble` records empty `judgeProvenance` and zero judge usage despite a completed, billable model call. Carry the completed attempt on cleanup failures (or handle close separately) so the failure envelope retains it.
findings.failureMode: Native judge completes and the credential-store close rejects; the ensemble reports a failed run with no judge attempts and zero known judge usage.
findings.title: Preserve a completed attempt when store cleanup fails

findings.description: When an exported `runEnsemble` caller supplies a lane result with `usage` omitted (or any non-null shape whose `total` is unavailable), `usageTotal(...) ?? 0` contributes zero but this check only rejects literal `null`. With otherwise valid lane and judge results the emitted record therefore says `usage.complete: true` even though lane usage is unknown. Determine completeness from the normalized usage total (or validate the lane usage shape) rather than `item.usage !== null`.
findings.failureMode: Injected or forward-compatible lane result omits a numeric usage total; ensemble reports complete token accounting with the missing usage counted as zero.
findings.title: Treat missing lane usage as incomplete

findings.description: For a development-calibration panel session, each authored finding is looked up in mustFix/waived, but the inverse and fingerprint uniqueness are never checked. Removing a real panel row from session.findings therefore validates and changes reported blocking families from 5 to 4 (precision 60% to 75%); duplicated mappings can likewise double-count repetition. Require an exact one-to-one inventory against the actual panel-record artifact.
findings.failureMode: A development panel result row is omitted or another row is duplicated during extraction; validation succeeds and published calibration metrics no longer represent the full panel output.
findings.title: Require exhaustive one-to-one panel mappings

findings.description: The inventory comparison checks only review IDs. If a raw GitHub item and the extracted artifact retain the same ID but have different bodies, both self-hashes validate and metrics continue using the artifact as evidence; a no-finding raw comment can therefore still yield a 100% Open SWE result. Compare each review, review-comment, and disposition artifact's content and metadata with its corresponding raw item.
findings.failureMode: A mis-extracted or edited artifact retains its ID and valid self-hash, passes validation, and supplies evidence that differs from the frozen authoritative response.
findings.title: Bind artifact content to the raw response

findings.description: Only the SHA format is checked. Assigning the same wrong 40-hex value to panel and Open SWE sessions still validates and phaseComparisons labels them phase-matched even though their primary review/panel artifacts name another commit. Compare each session head to the commit recorded by its authoritative source artifact.
findings.failureMode: Incorrectly extracted session heads make reviews of different or unknown commits appear phase-matched, producing an invalid overlap comparison.
findings.title: Bind reviewed heads to source artifacts

findings.description: Cross-round repetition uses sessions' record-array order and never reads priorSessionIds. Two parallel sessions with no declared ancestor relationship are therefore counted as repetitions, and branched/reordered histories are order-dependent. Derive seen-before families from each session's declared ancestors.
findings.failureMode: A later array entry repeats a family from an independent session but declares no prior; the report nevertheless increments crossRoundRepetitions.
findings.title: Use declared history for repetition metrics

findings.description: The final history check establishes only that prior IDs exist. A session can name itself, or two sessions can name each other, and validation succeeds even though the declared chronology is impossible. Add self-reference and graph-cycle validation.
findings.failureMode: A malformed corpus with a self-loop or history cycle is accepted as valid, so its declared chronological provenance cannot be true.
findings.title: Reject cyclic declared session histories

findings.description: The fixture names `context.input.baseSha` as its runtime-provenance source and populates `executingRuntimeSha` from it, but ingestion sets `baseSha` to GitHub's `merge_base_commit.sha`; elsewhere it is explicitly rendered as the repository's base revision. That SHA identifies the diff base, not the build running the panel. Under normal deploy/branch skew, `eval:continuity` and `eval:metrics` therefore attribute the run to the wrong executable, defeating the AC-7 output. Capture an executor/build SHA (or label this only as reviewed base provenance) instead.
findings.failureMode: A panel run executes deployment X for a PR whose merge base is Y; the report emits Y under `executingRuntimeSha`, falsely attributing the result to the wrong deployed code.
findings.title: Do not label the merge base as the executing runtime

findings.description: The fixture names `context.input.baseSha` as `runtimeProvenanceField` and relabels it as `executingRuntimeSha`, but `fetchPullRequestEvidence` sets that input from GitHub's `merge_base_commit.sha`. That value identifies the repository revision used to assemble the review, not the code deployed in the process. When a webhook runs during deployment lag (or against a branch with another merge base), both continuity commands will attribute the execution to the wrong build and may call a pre-deploy run post-deploy. Capture an actual runtime/deployment revision in the snapshot and derive these fields from it.
findings.failureMode: A normal panel run processed by a service whose deployed commit differs from the PR merge base is reported under the merge-base SHA, invalidating the runtime-provenance and post-deploy continuity result.
findings.title: Record the executing revision instead of the merge base

findings.description: The validator iterates source arrays without checking sequence or identity invariants even though aggregation depends on array order. Reversing the otherwise unchanged 13 runs is accepted and changes `crossRoundRepeatRate` from 70.4 to 73.5; duplicating round 1 is also accepted and inflates appearances to 109 and exact duplicates to 12. Duplicate Open SWE records likewise inflate `threads`. Require strictly ordered unique round/snapshot IDs and unique thread IDs before computing the report.
findings.failureMode: A custom or regenerated fixture containing out-of-order or duplicated source rows passes validation and publishes order-dependent or double-counted continuity metrics.
findings.title: Validate the canonical record sequence before aggregating

findings.description: Both regex guards call `RegExp.test` without first checking the value's type, so JSON one-element arrays containing a syntactically valid SHA or fingerprint pass by string coercion. An array-valued reviewed SHA is emitted unchanged in `perRound`, while separately parsed array-valued fingerprints are distinct Set keys and make `exactFingerprintDuplicates` report 0 for identical textual fingerprints. Require strings before both regex tests.
findings.failureMode: A custom continuity fixture with one-element array SHA/fingerprint values exits successfully with an invalid provenance shape or incorrect exact-duplicate metric instead of being rejected.
findings.title: Reject non-string SHA and fingerprint fields

findings.description: For the default `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` native judge, the provider reports its model in the `response.created` SSE event, but Mastra's completed output may retain only a synthesized/configured `response.modelId` and no `response.body.model`. This extractor examines only `response.body` (plus Claude metadata), so the successful generation and `runEnsemble` artifact record `modelReported: null` on the mainline default route even though provider identity was available. Capture provider-emitted OpenAI stream metadata at the fetch/provider boundary (without trusting the configured fallback) and include it here.
findings.failureMode: Run a normal golden ensemble with the default native OpenAI judge; the successful call's `GenerationCall.modelReported` and top-level `judgeModelReported` are null despite `response.created.response.model` being present, so evaluator provenance gives a wrong mainline identity result.
findings.title: Capture the native OpenAI model reported in the stream

findings.description: `judgePromptHash` is now the hash of the full successful attempt prompt, which includes each run's findings, context, and diff, so it changes across tags. `runBaseline` still treats this field as one baseline-wide value (`records.find(...).judgePromptHash`) and `runSummary` drops every run's hash. A normal multi-tag baseline therefore publishes the first tag's hash as the manifest's sole judge prompt hash even though it does not identify the other judge calls. Carry the exact hash/provenance in each run summary (and represent/validate the set at manifest level) rather than collapsing distinct prompts to the first one.
findings.failureMode: Run `certify.mjs baseline` for two tags with different diffs; the generated manifest contains only tag one's full-prompt hash and gives consumers the wrong prompt identity for tag two and the baseline as a whole.
findings.title: Keep per-run hashes when prompts now include run data

findings.description: Native Anthropic `Agent` results expose aggregate input in camel-case `inputTokens` plus `cachedInputTokens` and `cacheCreationInputTokens`. The flat fallback delegates to `normalizeUsage`, whose Anthropic detector recognizes only snake-case raw fields and whose non-Anthropic calculation subtracts cache reads but not cache writes. With provider usage `input_tokens=7`, `cache_read_input_tokens=3`, `cache_creation_input_tokens=2`, `output_tokens=5`, the new decision record becomes internally inconsistent (`input=9`, components sum to 19, `total=17`) instead of recording non-cache input 7. Normalize the nested/raw V3 details when present, or subtract both cache categories from the aggregate input.
findings.failureMode: Configure a supported native Anthropic adjudication or confirmation and receive any response with cache-creation tokens; the recorded generation usage overstates uncached input and downstream lower-bound/cost accounting is wrong.
findings.title: Subtract Anthropic cache writes from normalized input

findings.description: Raising the peer floor advertises Factory 0.10 compatibility, but 0.10 persists `model_provider_credentials.data` through `FactorySecretEncryption`; even its plaintext helper returns a JSON string. The unchanged glue store casts that raw JSONB value directly to `AuthCredential`, so after a normal re-login or credential save, the default native-reviewer preflight sees no `.type` and `factory-host` throws during startup (reproduced for both plaintext and AES envelopes). Use the same Factory encryption configuration to decrypt reads and encrypt refresh writes, or access credentials through the Factory domain API.
findings.failureMode: With an enabled native reviewer and a credential newly persisted by Factory 0.10, factory-host startup fails in native reviewer preflight because raw credential data is a string/encrypted envelope rather than an AuthCredential object.
findings.title: Decode Factory 0.10 credential envelopes

findings.description: This report describes the opposite result from the current-head experiment evidence in the PR metadata: it says baseline was 27/27 and the candidate regressed, while the corrected reset was baseline 25/27, candidate 27/27, precision 0.8333→0.9643, and controls 3→1. The table and gate section repeat the stale result and claim five failures rather than the sole cross-provider-gain failure. Although both runs yield “do not promote,” retaining this version gives future experiment readers the wrong measured behavior and rejection rationale; update the report to the corrected reset figures.
findings.failureMode: A developer consulting the retained experiment record concludes the candidate reduces recall/precision and causes more false positives, rather than recognizing its measured gains and the actual provider-diversity gate failure.
findings.title: Record the corrected reset result

findings.description: The three behavior tests reimplement `read`, the job rewrites, and provider pairing as local functions rather than reconstructing the modules recorded in `fixture.input.files`; only two account diff substrings and the file/label names are read from the fixture. Consequently `pnpm test:golden` passes on the current malformed hunk metadata and would also pass if `repositoryContent` or most frozen patches no longer had the asserted behavior. This makes the purported deterministic fixture validation produce a false green. Build and import before/after modules from the recorded patches, compare after-source to `repositoryContent`, and bind labels/snippets to those sources.
findings.failureMode: A malformed or behaviorally drifted frozen fixture passes the required golden test, so subsequent experiment replay uses a case different from the behavior the test claims to freeze.
findings.title: Execute the frozen modules instead of stand-ins

findings.description: The provider-rows header declares a 7-line/16-line hunk while its body contains 5 old and 15 new lines; its `+14 -5` metadata also disagrees with the 12 additions and 2 deletions actually present. This independently leaves the aggregate fixture corrupt and misstates the input shown to pack consumers. Correct both this entry and the duplicate aggregate hunk.
findings.failureMode: Reconstructing the provider-row positive from the frozen patch fails, so the advertised executable positive cannot be replayed.
findings.title: Correct the provider-rows patch metadata

findings.description: For `src/job-replacement.js`, the header records 13 old lines but the hunk body contains 11 (and the entry claims 11 deletions although only 9 `-` lines exist). A standard consumer cannot parse the frozen aggregate diff (`git apply --numstat` reports `corrupt patch`), so the retained experiment input is not independently executable or reproducible. Update this entry's header/diffstat and the duplicate hunk in `input.diff` to the actual counts.
findings.failureMode: Loading the retained fixture and passing `input.diff` to a normal unified-diff consumer fails instead of reconstructing the six cases.
findings.title: Correct the job-replacement hunk counts

findings.description: The provider-summary header declares 7 old and 18 new lines, but the hunk body has 5 and 17; the stored `+16 -5` diffstat likewise should reflect 14 additions and 2 deletions. This control's patch remains invalid independently of the other malformed entries. Correct this entry and its duplicate in `input.diff`.
findings.failureMode: Reconstructing the provider-summary negative control from the retained fixture fails at its malformed hunk.
findings.title: Correct the provider-summary patch metadata

findings.description: For `src/job-selection.js`, the header records 10 old lines but its body contains 9, and `deletions` says 8 although there are 7 removed lines. Even after the preceding malformed hunk is repaired, this remains another corrupt unified-diff hunk, preventing reconstruction of the frozen input. Update this entry and its duplicate in `input.diff`.
findings.failureMode: A normal unified-diff consumer rejects the selected-job control while reconstructing the retained experiment input.
findings.title: Correct the job-selection hunk counts

findings.description: The new exported continuity evaluator rounds exact half-tenths with `Math.round`, while the other golden-metrics percentage helpers use tie-to-even. A valid alternate continuity fixture selected through the CLI/API with one accepted family among 16 real families consequently reports 6.3% rather than the established evaluator result of 6.2%, producing a wrong metric at that boundary; use the existing tie-to-even calculation (or a shared helper).
findings.failureMode: For a valid selected continuity fixture whose percentage is exactly x.x5%, the evaluator emits a metric 0.1 percentage point too high versus the repository's established deterministic rounding contract.
findings.title: Use the evaluator's tie-to-even percentage rounding

findings.description: `evaluate` computes per-case correctness in `scores`, but also supplies `scoreVectors` containing only the two batch-wide must-fix metrics. AxGEPA prefers each `scoreVectors[i]` over `scores[i]`, so a candidate that returns the expected family/disposition set while getting every factual state, causal relation, consequence severity, and history state wrong receives the same `{mustFixPrecision:1, acceptedBlockerRetention:1}` optimization score as the known answers. Include row correctness (or the individual field scores) in the vectors so those advertised decisions affect optimization.
findings.failureMode: On a normal optimization batch, a candidate preserves only family IDs and delivery dispositions but misclassifies every other adjudication field; AxGEPA scores it identically to the all-correct candidate and may retain/select it.
findings.title: Include adjudication correctness in Ax score vectors

findings.description: The scorer maps every loaded case into a scored row without consulting `row.calibration.status`. The included `ordering-non-blocking` family is explicitly marked `excluded` because it lacks validated negative-control equivalence, yet `loadKnownAnswers()` returns it and the Ax test passes that full array to the adapter. As a result this excluded historical case contributes a normal 0/1 objective and can steer candidate selection, contrary to the corpus's exclusion. Preserve it for regression evidence, but omit excluded rows from calibration/optimizer scoring.
findings.failureMode: During the normal four-case Ax evaluation, any candidate that differs on the excluded job-selection case is penalized and can lose to a candidate tuned to that invalid calibration example.
findings.title: Exclude non-calibration cases from adjudication scores

findings.description: `reported` trusts only `familyId` and `deliveryDisposition` from every raw decision; it does not require a known/matching `caseId`, a matching input family, or a valid decision contract. Thus an omitted/misclassified blocker is still reported as retained if any other or unknown decision claims that blocker family with `must-fix`. The advertised hard retention constraint can therefore be green while the blocker case itself was dropped. Build the retained set only from valid decisions matched to their known case/family (or compare the expected blocker cases directly).
findings.failureMode: A candidate marks `hunk-metadata-must-fix` non-blocking but emits `familyId: fixture-hunk-metadata, deliveryDisposition: must-fix` for an unknown or different case; `acceptedBlockersRetained` incorrectly remains true.
findings.title: Bind blocker retention to the case that reported it

findings.description: The scorer intentionally matches decisions to cases by `caseId`, but the adapter's reflective `outputs` pairs each input with `decisions[index]` while taking failures from the scorer's case-ordered `score.rows[index]`. If adjudicator outputs arrive with unique but swapped/wrong case IDs, scores and failures are computed against the rematched decisions while the proposer is shown each decision beside the wrong input, including an empty failure list for a decision that belongs to another case. Return the scorer's matched decision per row (or enforce the returned case ID before appending) so reflection is truthful.
findings.failureMode: Two adjudication calls return each other's case IDs; scoring succeeds by ID, but reflective feedback shows decision B for input A and decision A for input B, causing the proposer to optimize from false examples.
findings.title: Keep rematched decisions paired with their cases

findings.description: `roundFingerprints` is recreated for each run, so identical fingerprints in later rounds are ignored. The checked-in fixture repeats `v1:7cfad…` in rounds 8 and 9, and `eval:continuity` consequently emits `exactFingerprintDuplicates: 0` rather than 1; keep a fixture-wide fingerprint set.
findings.failureMode: Running `pnpm eval:continuity` on the checked-in PR 195 fixture emits `panel.exactFingerprintDuplicates: 0` even though the same fingerprint appears in rounds 8 and 9.
findings.title: Count exact fingerprint duplicates across rounds

findings.description: The new script exposes continuity only through `eval:continuity`; `eval:metrics` still invokes the unchanged `metrics.mjs`, which has no continuity import or output. Thus the default optimizer-facing metrics command omits the new yield, repeat, duplicate, and calibration metrics.
findings.failureMode: Running `pnpm eval:metrics` after this change produces only the six pre-existing arm tables and no PR 195 continuity metrics.
findings.title: Include continuity in the default metrics command

findings.description: The panel appearance named `evidence-manifest-exposure` and Open SWE thread named `inner-run-manifest` describe the same omission, have the same reviewed head, and were resolved by the same `e93c665…` commit, yet the fixture gives them different family keys. Any family-level panel/Open SWE comparison therefore reports no shared defect instead of one.
findings.failureMode: A family overlap comparison over the checked-in fixture returns an empty intersection even though both systems found the inner-run evidence-manifest omission on `f637894…`.
findings.title: Canonicalize the shared manifest family

findings.description: The catalog check uses inherited object lookup, so undeclared names such as `toString` or `constructor` pass. An otherwise well-formed custom fixture is accepted and metrics are produced for a family absent from `families`; require an own-property check.
findings.failureMode: Invoking `eval:continuity` with an appearance family of `toString` and an empty family catalog exits 0 and reports one accepted family instead of rejecting the fixture.
findings.title: Reject inherited names as unknown families

findings.description: The changed test reclassifies `job-selection.js` as excluded historical evidence, but no corresponding exclusion reaches `scoreRun`. With the MASTRA-287 fixture and a single finding at `src/job-selection.js:2`, HEAD makes zero judge calls yet still reports `findings: 1`, `precision_strict: 0`, `notScored: []`, and includes the finding in feedback. The invalid control therefore continues to depress benchmark precision and enter optimization feedback despite the claimed quarantine. Apply the fixture-local exact tag/file exclusion before candidate generation and every downstream metric/feedback path, preserving the removed row in an `excludedFindings`-style field.
findings.failureMode: For tag 287, a lane output containing the proven `src/job-selection.js` ordering finding is counted as a false positive and included in feedback/optimization rather than quarantined.
findings.title: Quarantine is not applied at the scoring boundary

findings.description: Both cache cases depend on `Client.read` defaulting `cache` to true, but the fixture supplies `src/client.js` only in `repositoryContent`. Production `assembleContext` selects content through the changed-file inventory, where `src/client.js` is absent; the rendered lane context contains neither the class nor `cache = true`. Thus reviewers cannot ground the account positive or disprove the preference control's “might become uncached” finding—the exact finding the report penalizes as invalid based on an implementation the reviewer was never shown. This makes the measured hits and strict precision evidence-incomplete. Include the `Client.read` default explicitly in the fixture's rendered context.
findings.failureMode: Every lane hides the source needed both to prove the account regression and to refute the preference control finding, so the experiment's hit and precision counts judge answers against unavailable evidence.
findings.title: Client default is hidden from every lane

findings.description: The frozen `src/job-selection.js` control is not behavior-preserving: the old loop interleaves `registry.has(job.kind)` with `registry.create(job)`, while `.filter(...).map(...)` runs every `has` before any `create`. For two known jobs and a registry whose first `create` disables the kind, the before version creates only the first job, but the after version admits and creates both. This is precisely the experiment's registered ordering/side-effect check, yet the file is declared a negative control and has no label, so a correct reviewer finding is counted as invalid and skews precision. Rewrite this control to preserve per-job `has`/`create` interleaving.
findings.failureMode: With a registry where create changes what has returns for later dense-array jobs, the before and after job-selection versions return different replacements despite this source being treated as an equivalent negative control.
findings.title: Negative control changes callback ordering

findings.description: The frozen `src/provider-summary.js` control turns one `Object.entries` pass into two independent passes, so each provider's `enabled` property is read twice instead of once. With an ordinary config object whose `enabled` accessor returns true on its first read and false on its second, the before version returns `{ name: 'p', token: 'T' }`, while the after version returns `{ name: 'p', token: undefined }`. This is an ordering/side-effect behavior change covered by the registered lens, yet the source is declared a negative control and omitted from labels, so a correct reviewer finding is counted as invalid. Capture the provider entries and enabled state once before deriving both arrays.
findings.failureMode: A provider config with a stateful `enabled` accessor is read once before the patch but twice after it, producing a mismatched name/token row in the supposedly equivalent control.
findings.title: Negative control reads provider state twice

findings.description: The live CLI accepts `--plan`, `--ledger`, and `--report` without proving they are distinct. If `--report` names the ledger (including via a relative or symlink alias), execution succeeds and the final `writeFile` replaces the append-only ledger with the summary; if it names the plan, it destroys the registered plan instead. Resolve and compare all three targets before opening or writing any of them.
findings.failureMode: A live run invoked with report and ledger/plan paths resolving to the same file succeeds, then overwrites an immutable audit artifact.
findings.title: Reject aliased live artifact paths

findings.description: A `micro-pilot-result` bypasses the failed/incomplete checks and reaches Ax before any inventory validation. If a cached `adjudication` row is missing, Ax calls the harness again and only then does line 89 reject on `calls.cursor`; if terminal rows or `prior.report` are damaged instead, replay can still return success with unsupported call/usage claims. Validate the exact intent/terminal/replay-row inventory and recompute the report before entering Ax for a completed ledger.
findings.failureMode: A damaged completed ledger either causes a duplicate paid provider request before rejection or is accepted with false audit/accounting output.
findings.title: Fail closed before replaying a damaged result ledger

findings.description: The retry guard calls a run incomplete only when an intent has no terminal. If the process dies after the succeeded terminal is fsynced in `invoke` but before `AdjudicationAdapter` appends its replayable adjudication/proposal row, the ledger has no failure and no unterminated intent, so the next invocation starts at operation 1 and pays for it again. The retry can then finish with two terminals for op-01 and an `actualCalls` total of six despite the five-call plan. Refuse this state or recover the result without another provider call.
findings.failureMode: A crash between terminal and replay-row appends lets an in-place retry issue a duplicate paid request and preserve a six-call run as valid.
findings.title: Refuse retry after an uncommitted successful call

findings.description: When line 83 detects an existing failed or incomplete ledger, it throws `failed-ledger`, but this catch immediately appends another `micro-pilot-failure` because `prior` is absent and `ledger.rows.length` is nonzero. Merely retrying a preserved failed run therefore changes its bytes and invalidates any recorded file hash. Do not journal a new failure when refusing an already-used ledger.
findings.failureMode: Re-running the CLI against a failed ledger mutates the supposedly immutable evidence file and breaks its hash binding.
findings.title: Keep failed-ledger refusal byte-preserving

findings.description: This derives `currentRevision` with `git rev-parse` but never checks `git status --porcelain`. With modified fixture, prompt, adapter, or harness files in the working tree, both plan reconstruction and live execution can use those uncommitted bytes while the manifest and report attribute them to the clean HEAD SHA. Perform the same clean-clone preflight already used by `pilot.mjs` before dry-run planning and live execution.
findings.failureMode: Running the CLI from a dirty checkout records an execution as belonging to HEAD even though uncommitted code/data determined the plan or result.
findings.title: Refuse dirty source before attributing the run

findings.description: The two cleanup awaits are sequential in one `finally`. If the credential store/harness `close()` rejects, `ledger.close()` is skipped, the original run result/error is replaced by the cleanup error, and the `.lock` remains owned by the still-live process so another call in that process is refused. Put ledger release in its own nested `finally` (while preserving the primary error).
findings.failureMode: A reachable harness/store close rejection leaks the ledger lock and turns a completed run into a cleanup failure.
findings.title: Always release the ledger lock when harness close fails

findings.description: This new API-key rewrite path sends a previous-key API row through `refreshLocked`. If a concurrent transaction holds and then deletes that row, the lock attempt times out and every recovery read has `fresh.selected === undefined`; the method waits through all retries and throws `lock wait timed out without a usable row` instead of clearing the snapshot and returning `undefined` as the non-timeout locked-deletion path does. Handle an absent recovery result as a concurrent deletion so rotating API-key reads do not become 30-second errors.
findings.failureMode: A previous-key API credential is concurrently deleted by the lock holder; getApiKey throws after the retry window instead of reporting no credential.
findings.title: Treat deletion during API-key rewrite recovery as absence

findings.description: When the selected credential is OAuth but `getOAuthProvider(provider)` returns undefined, this branch returns before checking whether any row needs a primary-key rewrite. A previous-key candidate (including a shadowed API-key row) is therefore left encrypted with the retiring key; after that key is removed, resolving the provider throws `decrypt_failed` even if the unsupported OAuth row has been removed and the shadowed row should become usable. Run the locked rotation independently of provider availability (rewriting even an unusable expired OAuth value unchanged), and only return `undefined` after the rotation commits.
findings.failureMode: An unknown/unregistered OAuth row shadows a previous-key candidate; getApiKey skips rotation, then key retirement makes the remaining candidate unreadable.
findings.title: Rotate old-key rows before rejecting an unknown OAuth provider

findings.description: This test configures the credential store but never clears `FACTORY_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` or `_KEY_ID`; `vi.unstubAllEnvs()` restores any ambient values rather than removing them. On a developer/CI host that legitimately exports the Factory keyring for native/eval tests, the import gets past `createRequiredCredentialEncryption` and fails later for unrelated missing boot variables, so this assertion fails nondeterministically. Stub both encryption vars to empty in this test before importing.
findings.failureMode: Running the suite with Factory encryption keys exported makes the new missing-key boot test fail for the wrong reason.
findings.title: Explicitly clear encryption vars in the missing-key test

findings.description: The fixture declares `context.input.baseSha` to be the runtime-provenance source and uses it for every `executingRuntimeSha`, but production ingestion populates `baseSha` from the PR comparison's `mergeBaseSha`. That is the commit against which the diff is built, not an identifier emitted by the running deployment; existing evaluation pins record the deployed commit separately. Consequently these outputs do not establish AC-7 runtime provenance and become wrong whenever studio2 is not running the PR's merge base. Capture the deployed/runtime artifact SHA from a runtime-owned source instead.
findings.failureMode: For a panel run executed by a studio2 deployment whose code revision differs from the PR merge base, the emitted `executingRuntimeSha` identifies the merge base rather than the code that executed the run, producing false provenance in the main evaluation output.
findings.title: Do not relabel the PR merge base as the executing runtime

findings.description: The guard enforces `real` only for accepted appearances, even though this metric treats a deferred family as a real unresolved defect (the frozen slice is explicitly 18 accepted plus one deferred). If that deferred family's `real` flag is false, validation succeeds, `deferredFamilies` still reports one, but the yield denominator drops it and inflates 18/19 to 18/18 (100%). Require deferred appearances, not just accepted ones, to belong to real families.
findings.failureMode: A fixture with a deferred appearance whose family is marked `real: false` passes validation and publishes an inflated unique-accepted-family yield.
findings.title: Reject deferred appearances assigned to non-real families

findings.description: The job-replacement patch declares `@@ -1,13 +1,5 @@` and `deletions: 11`, but its body contains only 11 old-side lines and 9 deletions. The same mismatch recurs for job-selection and both provider patches, plus the copies in `input.diff`; `git apply --check` rejects the aggregate at line 35 as corrupt. The production repository pack also renders these false additions/deletions in its headings, so this changes the actual reviewer context and pack hash. The checked-in fixture is therefore not the corrected, independently executable input the experiment report claims. Regenerate all hunk ranges and additions/deletions counts from the patch bodies in both representations and rerun against those bytes.
findings.failureMode: Applying or validating tag 287's supposedly executable frozen diff fails as corrupt, and lane reviewers receive false file-size metadata, so the committed input cannot reproduce the claimed corrected run.
findings.title: Regenerate the malformed frozen patch metadata

findings.description: This ingest snapshot stores a raw `diff --git` document in `input.diff`, while production snapshots and `auditVisibility` use the aggregate `Patches:\n### <path>\n<hunk>` form to associate changed lines with files. Running the standard visibility audit (after supplying the separately required raw diff) reports all three tag-287 labels as `notVisible` because no `###` file marker is ever seen. Any functional-only scoring path that consumes that audit therefore excludes the entire positive cohort. Serialize `input.diff` from the six file patches in the production aggregate format and retain the raw git diff separately for scorer hunks.
findings.failureMode: Visibility/audit-driven evaluation sees zero visible functional labels for tag 287 and can score a candidate without any of the three intended positives, producing invalid recall and gate results.
findings.title: Use the production aggregate format for `input.diff`

findings.description: Registering `287` as a train tag makes it loadable by `loadLaneFixture`, but the production scorer's `scoreRun` calls `loadFrozenDiff(fixtures, run.tag)` for any run with a tier-1 candidate, which requires exactly one `phase-a/dataset/diffs/287_*.diff`. This fixture tree contains no such directory/file, and the call fails with `ENOENT`, so the committed artifacts cannot reproduce the reported 18 scorer runs. Add the frozen raw git diff at the scorer's expected path.
findings.failureMode: Scoring a tag-287 lane record containing an anchored finding aborts before the semantic judge with ENOENT, preventing reproduction of recall and precision metrics.
findings.title: Provide the scorer's frozen diff for tag 287

findings.description: This report still describes the invalidated run (baseline 27/27, candidate 26/27, lower precision, and five failed gates), whereas the PR's final reset evidence says the corrected inputs produced 25/27 to 27/27, precision 0.8333 to 0.9643, fewer invalid control findings, and only the cross-provider-gains condition failed. The recorded pack hash also matches the currently malformed metadata; recomputing after correcting those counts changes it from `3e88...` to `3a33...`. Although both runs lead to non-promotion, merging this version publishes the wrong experiment result and rationale. Replace the decision, hashes, table, analysis, and gate application with the corrected 36-record reset.
findings.failureMode: Future prompt experiments consuming this durable report treat a demonstrated recall/precision improvement as a regression and apply the wrong baseline, hashes, and failure analysis.
findings.title: Replace the invalidated run in the experiment report

findings.description: The behavior tests create local `read`, `before`/`after`, and provider implementations rather than deriving and executing the source in `fixture.input.files`/`repositoryContent`. For example, changing the frozen `Client.read` default to `false` leaves all four tests green even though the preferences control and account label reverse meaning. Thus the test added to `test:golden` does not validate the artifact actually fed to reviewers and can certify a corrupted cohort. Reconstruct each before/after module from the recorded patch, execute those exports, and assert the reconstructed after source exactly equals its `repositoryContent` entry.
findings.failureMode: A fixture source or patch drifts away from the hand-copied test implementation; CI remains green while the reviewer lane exercises different behavior and the golden labels/controls are invalid.
findings.title: Execute the frozen modules instead of hard-coded stand-ins

findings.description: The default native OpenAI judge reports its served model in the `response.created` SSE event. The pinned Agent exposes that provider value as `response.modelId` (separately from `response.modelMetadata.modelId`, the configured identity), but this extractor ignores both and only checks `response.body` plus Claude metadata. Consequently successful native adjudications record `modelReported: null`; capture the trusted SSE/modelId evidence without substituting a configured fallback.
findings.failureMode: Every successful default native OpenAI judge call loses the provider-reported model identity and publishes null in both attempt provenance and ensemble judgeModelReported.
findings.title: Capture native OpenAI's reported model

findings.description: For the camelCase usage shape returned by the native Anthropic Agent, `inputTokens` includes uncached, cache-read, and cache-write tokens (the pinned stack returns 12 for 7 + 3 + 2). This branch subtracts only cache reads, so a decision emits `input: 9` rather than 7 and its components sum to 19 while `total` is 17. Subtract both `cached` and `cacheCreation` for the normalized camelCase shape.
findings.failureMode: A normal Anthropic decision that creates prompt-cache tokens reports inflated uncached input usage, corrupting per-category evaluator/cost metrics.
findings.title: Subtract cache writes from normalized input

findings.description: This changes `judgePromptHash` from the shared adjudication-instruction hash to the exact invocation hash, which varies with each run's findings, context, and diff. `runBaseline` still drops the field from every run summary and publishes only `records.find(...).judgePromptHash`; with two hashes (`exact-001` and `exact-002`) the manifest keeps only `exact-001`. Carry each exact hash into its run summary and do not present one arbitrary invocation hash as baseline-wide provenance.
findings.failureMode: A normal multi-tag baseline emits one top-level hash from the first judge call while omitting every later call's distinct hash, producing incorrect provenance for the baseline artifact.
findings.title: Keep per-run judge hashes in the baseline manifest

findings.description: The numeric normalizer accepts every finite number rather than non-negative integer token counts. Native xAI responses with malformed negative or fractional usage pass the pinned provider stack and are published as negative/fractional usage, so evaluator and cost totals become invalid while `usage.status` remains complete. Require non-negative safe integers and return null for malformed usage before aggregation.
findings.failureMode: An untrusted provider response with negative or fractional token counters is accepted and produces invalid aggregate usage/cost metrics.
findings.title: Validate provider token counters

findings.description: The normalizer validates each component with Number.isSafeInteger but adds them without validating the sum; addUsage repeats the same unchecked arithmetic. If an untrusted provider reports individually safe counts whose sum exceeds Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (for example inputTokens=MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and outputTokens=2), the recorded total is rounded instead of exact, and aggregation can still label the result complete. Reject unsafe component sums as unknown/incomplete, including aggregate additions.
findings.failureMode: Untrusted provider usage counts that are individually safe but overflow when summed produce rounded, falsely complete usage provenance.
findings.title: Reject totals that overflow safe integers

findings.description: When an expired selected OAuth row has any shadowed row needing a primary-key rewrite, the code refreshes the external rotating token first and then performs every candidate write. A failure sealing or updating the shadow row rolls the whole transaction back after the IdP invalidated the old refresh token, so the database retains only an unusable token and all later native authentication fails. Complete the fallible shadow rewrites before calling `refreshToken`, or persist the refreshed selected credential independently.
findings.failureMode: An expired selected OAuth row plus a shadowed previous-key row and a write/seal failure on the shadow rewrite rolls back the freshly rotated credential, leaving only an invalid old refresh token persisted.
findings.title: Rewrite shadow rows before rotating the selected OAuth token

findings.description: This new API-key rewrite path enters `refreshLocked`, whose retry-read catch still reports an OAuth refresh failure. With a previous-key API credential, a lock timeout followed by a failed recovery read therefore emits a false OAuth diagnosis even though no OAuth credential or provider exists, sending operators toward the wrong remediation. Make that recovery error operation-neutral, as the final timeout error already is.
findings.failureMode: A previous-key API credential plus lock timeout and failed recovery read emits a false OAuth refresh error, sending operators toward the wrong remediation.
findings.title: Do not label API-key recovery as OAuth refresh

findings.description: This makes the native OpenAI adjudicator the default, but that adjudicator returns only `result.object` and never checks the response's model identity; `runWithFallback` then records the requested `gpt-5.6-sol` as `usedModel`. If the OAuth endpoint aliases, deprecates, or otherwise serves a different model, the panel accepts and publishes that model's verdict as a Sol verdict instead of failing closed. The existing native `generateText` path already rejects missing/mismatched `response.modelId`; add equivalent served-identity validation to native adjudication before routing default panel decisions through it.
findings.failureMode: A non-Sol OpenAI response is accepted and published as the default Sol panel verdict.
findings.title: Verify the served model before making native Sol the default

findings.description: With `PANEL_JUDGE_HARNESS=claude`, `PANEL_JUDGE_FALLBACK_HARNESS=native`, and `PANEL_JUDGE_NATIVE_MODEL` unset, the server now assigns the policy's Sol default to that native fallback, but the golden evaluator leaves `nativeModel` undefined because this condition only checks the primary. If Claude fails, `runWithFallback` records a native target/config failure instead of running the Sol fallback, so certification/replay can report a failed judge for a configuration that production serves. Derive the default whenever either selected judge harness is native (while preserving the server's distinction between unset and explicitly blank values).
findings.failureMode: A custom Claude-primary/native-fallback evaluation fails instead of recovering through the default native Sol route.
findings.title: Default the native model when native is the fallback

findings.description: For the default native judge, `PANEL_JUDGE_NATIVE_MODEL=''` is explicitly invalid in the server (`index.ts` distinguishes `undefined` from a blank value and the changed boot test requires rejection), but this `trim() || default` expression silently turns that same setting into `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`. A golden baseline or fidelity replay can therefore succeed and emit Sol results under configuration that production cannot boot. Mirror the server's undefined-vs-blank handling and fail the evaluator for an explicitly blank native model.
findings.failureMode: Golden evaluation succeeds with Sol while the corresponding production configuration fails at startup.
findings.title: Do not reinterpret an explicitly blank native model

findings.description: `roundFingerprints` is recreated for each run, so the duplicate check only detects repeats within one round. In the frozen fixture, fingerprint `v1:7cfad00d...d64a2` appears in rounds 8 and 9, yet `eval:continuity` reports `exactFingerprintDuplicates: 0`; this makes the main continuity metric wrong. Keep a fixture-wide fingerprint set (or explicitly compare against prior rounds) so the cross-round duplicate is reported as 1.
findings.failureMode: Running `pnpm eval:continuity` on the added PR-195 fixture reports zero exact fingerprint duplicates even though the same fingerprint occurs in rounds 8 and 9.
findings.title: Count exact fingerprints across rounds

findings.description: The fixture declares `context.input.baseSha` as its runtime provenance and copies that value into `executingRuntimeSha`, but `fetchPullRequestEvidence` fills `baseSha` from `compareCommitsWithBasehead(...).merge_base_commit.sha`. That is the reviewed diff's merge base, not the revision of the process executing the panel. A lagging deployment or non-default target therefore makes this evaluation report the wrong runtime and falsely satisfy the runtime-provenance criterion; freeze actual deployment/build metadata per run instead.
findings.failureMode: A run executed by deployment X for a PR whose merge base is Y is reported as having executing runtime Y.
findings.title: Do not relabel the PR merge base as runtime provenance

findings.description: The Open SWE thread reviewed at `8579b...` is assigned `pending-authoritative-replay`, while the panel appearance on that same reviewed head is assigned the registered `authoritative-replay` family. Thus the default fixture's panel/Open-SWE family intersection is empty and comparison code treats the shared replay defect as unrelated. Assign the Open SWE thread the same canonical family key.
findings.failureMode: Comparing family keys in the default fixture reports zero shared panel/Open-SWE defects instead of one.
findings.title: Use one family for the shared replay defect

findings.description: The changed test only retains `src/job-selection.js` and confirms that it has no positive label; the fixture tree contains no exclusion metadata, and `scoreRun` still passes every surfaced finding directly into scoring. Consequently, a MASTRA-287 run with the now-proven `src/job-selection.js` finding is still emitted in feedback and scored as one false positive (`findings: 1`, `precision_strict: 0`) rather than being removed before candidate generation, judging, metrics, and feedback. Add the exact tag/file exclusion sidecar and enforce it at the scoring boundary.
findings.failureMode: Scoring a MASTRA-287 run containing an exact `src/job-selection.js` finding still penalizes benchmark precision and includes the quarantined finding in downstream feedback.
findings.title: Apply the exclusion before scoring

findings.description: For the default native OpenAI judge, the AI SDK derives `result.response.modelId` from the provider's `response.created.model`. When that value is exactly `gpt-5.6-sol`, this inequality discards it, so a successful mainline generation and the ensemble emit `modelReported: null` even though the provider supplied the identity. A probe that changed only `response.created.model` showed `result.response.modelId` changing with it. Distinguish the Claude wrapper's synthesized `modelId` from native AI-SDK results (or capture the SSE model directly) rather than treating equality itself as absence of evidence.
findings.failureMode: A successful default native OpenAI adjudication reports `gpt-5.6-sol`, but its provenance and ensemble output claim the reported identity is unavailable.
findings.title: Preserve equal provider-reported native model IDs

findings.description: Registering `287` as a train tag makes this root loadable by the lane/scoring workflow, but the root has no `phase-a/dataset/diffs/287_*.diff`. `scoreRun` and the `match.mjs` CLI call `loadFrozenDiff` whenever a finding is near a label, so any substantive tag-287 lane aborts with `ENOENT` before producing metrics. Commit the aggregate diff at the standard dataset path (and bind it to the ingest diff) so the retained labeled fixture can actually be rescored.
findings.failureMode: Score a tag-287 lane result containing an account, disposal, or provider finding through `match.mjs --fixtures evals/golden/fixtures/mastra-287`: candidate generation succeeds, then loading the missing dataset directory throws ENOENT and no score is written.
findings.title: Provide the frozen diff required by the scorer

findings.description: `src/client.js` is stored only in `repositoryContent`, but `assembleLaneContext` passes `input.files` as the renderer inventory, and the renderer selects only fetched paths in that inventory. Thus every tag-287 lane omits the `Client.read` implementation. Reviewers see `cache: false`/`cache: true` disappear but cannot see that omission defaults to `true`; earning the account positive requires guessing hidden behavior, while rejecting the preference control requires the same hidden fact. The recorded runs actually produced the corresponding preference false positive, so scoring it as invalid uses an oracle fact absent from the model input and invalidates the reported precision/recall comparison. Put the default contract in reviewer-visible context (or otherwise make the unchanged dependency visible), then rerun and validate the actual assembled lane context.
findings.failureMode: Run either removed-option case through tag 287: production context assembly reports neither `class Client` nor `cache = true`, so a contract-compliant reviewer cannot establish which removal changes behavior; at least one recorded run guessed the control incorrectly, yet scoring classified it from hidden evidence.
findings.title: Expose the hidden cache default to lane reviewers

findings.description: The fixture names `context.input.baseSha` as its executing-runtime provenance source, but GitHub ingestion populates `baseSha` from `comparison.data.merge_base_commit.sha`. If the deployed panel revision differs from a PR's merge base, the continuity report labels the merge base as the executing runtime and emits incorrect AC-7 provenance. Record an independently captured deployment/build SHA instead.
findings.failureMode: For a panel run executed by deployment D against a PR whose merge base is B, the fixture/output reports B as `executingRuntimeSha` even though D executed the run.
findings.title: Do not use the PR merge base as runtime provenance

findings.description: The validator accepts either authority string without checking `githubReviewId`, even though the fixture uses the absence of a published GitHub review to distinguish the pending replay from 12 authoritative runs. A run with `githubReviewId: null` and `authority: 'authoritative'` is accepted and counted as authoritative, recreating the misclassification this slice is meant to prevent. Require authoritative runs to carry a review ID and pending-replay runs not to.
findings.failureMode: A stored successful run has no GitHub review publication but is labeled authoritative; evaluation succeeds and reports an inflated authoritative run count instead of a pending replay.
findings.title: Tie run authority to publication evidence

findings.description: `panelFamilies` includes every catalog key, including families explicitly marked `real: false` for rejected panel claims. If an Open SWE thread uses one of those family labels, `sharedPanelFamilies` reports it as a shared concrete defect even though the panel classification says it is not real. Build the overlap set only from families whose panel classification has `real: true`.
findings.failureMode: A valid comparison fixture maps an Open SWE finding to a panel family classified `real: false`; the evaluator falsely reports that rejected claim as a shared panel/Open SWE defect.
findings.title: Exclude rejected panel claims from shared-family overlap

findings.description: The classification guard rejects only `accepted` appearances for `real: false` families, but a deferred disposition also denotes a real defect (the fixture's deferred publication-idempotency family is real and deferred to a ticket). A malformed fixture can therefore defer a rejected/non-real claim and still be scored, producing a deferred-family count outside the real-family denominator. Require every non-rejected appearance to belong to a real family.
findings.failureMode: A fixture marks a `real: false` family appearance as `deferred`; validation succeeds and metrics report one deferred family but zero real families, yielding internally invalid continuity output.
findings.title: Reject deferred appearances for non-real families

findings.description: `assertFixture` checks only the synthetic round numbers and never enforces unique `snapshotRunId` values. A copied source run can therefore be assigned the next round number, pass validation, and have every appearance counted again here, inflating adjudication, blocking, repeat, and calibration metrics. Validate source-run identity uniqueness before aggregation.
findings.failureMode: A custom fixture accidentally contains the same panel snapshot twice under consecutive round numbers; evaluation succeeds and double-counts the run.
findings.title: Reject duplicate panel run records before aggregation

findings.description: The public fixture-path entry point validates that each thread has a family but never enforces unique thread IDs, while this line reports raw array length as the number of threads. A fixture containing the same Open SWE thread twice is accepted and reports two threads instead of one, corrupting the comparison metrics. Reject duplicate IDs during fixture validation before counting records.
findings.failureMode: A custom continuity fixture repeats one `openSweThreads` record; evaluation succeeds and inflates `openSwe.threads`.
findings.title: Reject duplicate Open SWE thread IDs

findings.description: The source-backed comparison filters to review and review-comment artifacts only, so operator-disposition artifacts—the evidence used to assign factual state and delivery disposition—are checked only against their own editable hash. If a record changes an operator comment (and its contentSha256) or substitutes another comment ID while retaining the separately frozen issue-comments response, validation still succeeds and the precision/disposition metrics can report fabricated adjudications. Project the raw issue-comments response and compare every operator-disposition artifact just as the review artifacts are compared.
findings.failureMode: A tampered or incorrectly extracted operator disposition remains accepted as source-backed and changes calibration metrics despite disagreeing with the frozen GitHub issue-comment bytes.
findings.title: Bind operator dispositions to raw issue-comment bytes

findings.description: Unlike panel sessions, the Open SWE branch only asks whether each referenced comment contains `🟡`; it never enforces uniqueness or that every finding comment is represented. One yellow source comment can therefore be reused for multiple different family rows (or an actual comment can be omitted) while validation succeeds, changing both the Open SWE and combined precision. Parse the embedded finding identity and require an exhaustive one-to-one mapping for development-calibration Open SWE sessions.
findings.failureMode: A duplicate or omitted extracted Open SWE finding passes validation and causes the report to overcount or undercount accepted/reported families relative to the frozen GitHub review.
findings.title: Bind Open SWE findings one-to-one to source comments

findings.description: The exhaustive check proves only that the hand-authored session rows agree with the hand-authored panel-record artifact; it never ties that artifact's run URL or finding inventory back to the frozen GitHub review. A panel-record payload, its hash, and matching session/family rows can be changed together while the authoritative review still advertises the original run and finding count, and validation accepts the resulting altered precision. For published sessions, verify the panel artifact identity/run URL and published inventory against the bound review artifact (while retaining the explicit snapshot exception).
findings.failureMode: A full panel record from the wrong run, or a locally altered record plus matching derived rows, validates and changes panel metrics despite contradicting the frozen published review.
findings.title: Bind panel records to the published review source

findings.description: The validator checks only that record.source SHAs look syntactically valid; the raw `:pull` response is hashed but never compared with record.pullRequest, source.baseSha/headSha/mergeSha, URL, or merged state. A mislabeled record can therefore pass and have sessions and findings attributed to the wrong PR/head in inventory and phase comparisons even though the authoritative frozen pull bytes disagree. Parse the required pull source and bind those record fields to it.
findings.failureMode: A record copied under the wrong manifest PR or populated with the wrong source SHAs validates and produces metrics attributed to an incorrect pull request/revision.
findings.title: Verify record identity against the frozen pull response

findings.description: On the default native OpenAI judge path, the Responses stream emits `response-metadata.modelId` from `response.created.response.model`. When that reported value is the normal exact requested ID (`gpt-5.6-sol`), this inequality drops it, so the successful attempt and `judgeModelReported` are null even though the provider supplied the identity. Treat the native response metadata as evidence even when it equals the request (while separately excluding fields known to be configuration echoes).
findings.failureMode: A successful default OpenAI judge response reports model `gpt-5.6-sol`; provenance records `modelReported: null`, producing wrong mainline evaluator identity output.
findings.title: Preserve an exact provider-reported model ID

findings.description: `PanelResult.waived` contains `{ finding, reason, basis }` objects, not findings, so a waived row has no top-level `fingerprint` or `severity`. A valid waived result with no must-fix items and `blocking: false` is rejected as `Panel finding drift`. Normalize waived entries with `result.waived.map(item => item.finding)` before matching and use membership in the normalized must-fix list for the blocking check.
findings.failureMode: A valid development-calibration session containing a waived panel finding cannot be loaded or measured.
findings.title: Unwrap waived findings before matching

findings.description: Panel reviews expose valid non-blocking findings through `result.adjudications` (confirmed below threshold or plausible), as the production renderer does, but this matcher searches only `mustFix` and `waived`. A confirmed low finding under a medium threshold, retained only in adjudications and marked non-blocking in the session, is rejected as drift. Include reportable non-blocking adjudications in the normalized source inventory; otherwise `validNonBlockingPreservation` cannot measure the normal non-blocking panel path.
findings.failureMode: A calibrated panel session with an ordinary confirmed/plausible non-blocking finding is rejected, preventing the advertised preservation metric from being populated.
findings.title: Include non-blocking adjudications in panel matching

findings.description: For a development-calibration panel session, this loop only proves that each declared session finding can be found in `mustFix`/`waived`; it never proves the reverse or prevents two finding IDs from reusing one fingerprint. Deleting the PR 194 session finding is therefore accepted and changes reported blocking from 5 to 4 and precision from 60% to 75%; duplicating it is also accepted and invents a within-round duplicate. Compare the session finding fingerprints one-to-one and exhaustively with the source panel record's reportable findings.
findings.failureMode: A missing or duplicated extracted panel finding passes validation and produces incorrect calibration and repetition metrics.
findings.title: Require a bijection with panel output findings

findings.description: This check validates only findings that were already copied into `session.findings`; it never requires each development-calibration yellow review comment in the session to have a corresponding finding. Deleting PR 196's sole Open SWE finding is accepted, reducing the combined headline from 3/5 (60%) to 2/4 (50%) while Open SWE still misleadingly reports 100% precision. Build a one-to-one inventory between calibrated yellow source comments and session findings, including the structured comment ID/anchor.
findings.failureMode: An omitted Open SWE finding silently changes the published calibration metrics while the corpus still validates.
findings.title: Require every calibrated Open SWE comment to be represented

findings.description: `seenBefore` is the union of every previously iterated session for the PR/system, not the sessions named in the current session's `priorSessionIds`. Consequently independent sessions are counted as cross-round repeats solely because of array order. Removing the PR 200 later panel session's only declared predecessor is accepted and `crossRoundRepetitions` remains 1. Resolve the current session's declared ancestor IDs and derive prior families from those sessions instead.
findings.failureMode: The published declared-history repetition count includes findings from sessions that are not in the session's declared history.
findings.title: Compute repetitions from declared ancestry

findings.description: The second pass checks only that every `priorSessionIds` target exists in the record. A self-reference, and likewise a multi-session cycle, is accepted even though the corpus is supposed to validate acyclic prior-session history. Traverse the prior-session graph and reject self and cyclic ancestry before accepting the corpus.
findings.failureMode: A corpus with cyclic session provenance is reported as valid, so history-backed calibration can be published from an impossible session chronology.
findings.title: Reject cycles in declared session history

findings.description: This inventory comparison checks only review IDs extracted from the hashed GitHub responses. It never checks that a review artifact's `content` and `commitSha` equal that raw item's `body` and `commit_id`, and operator-disposition artifacts are not inventoried at all. Replacing the calibrated Open SWE comment body with `🟡 fabricated`, or replacing an operator disposition, and recomputing the independent artifact hash leaves the raw source untouched but still passes validation. Validate every extracted GitHub artifact's fields against the corresponding parsed raw item, not just review IDs.
findings.failureMode: Altered extracted review or disposition evidence passes corpus validation despite disagreeing with the frozen authoritative GitHub response.
findings.title: Bind extracted artifacts to raw source bytes

findings.description: A session's `reviewedHeadSha` is only format-checked and is never compared with the commit SHA of its authoritative review/panel artifact. Replacing PR 194's panel head with an unrelated valid SHA is accepted; the overall precision still reports 60% while only the phase comparison becomes `unvalidated`. This allows a calibrated session to contribute to the headline metrics under false head provenance. Require the session head to match the session's primary review or panel-record commit before including it in calibration.
findings.failureMode: A session attributed to the wrong code revision remains in the development-calibration metrics.
findings.title: Verify each reviewed head against its session evidence

findings.description: The source SHAs are merely checked for hex shape even though the hashed `github:<pr>:pull` response contains the authoritative `base.sha`, `head.sha`, and `merge_commit_sha`. Changing `record.source.headSha` to 40 zeroes leaves the raw pull bytes unchanged and still validates. Compare the extracted source fields (and PR identity) to the parsed pull response so the manifest cannot certify false PR provenance.
findings.failureMode: A corpus record with a fabricated base, head, or merge revision is accepted as authoritative source evidence.
findings.title: Bind PR source metadata to the raw pull response

findings.description: Finding validation checks that the source artifact belongs to the session but never aligns its calibration status with the development-calibration session. Marking PR 196's actual finding comment `excluded` (with the required exclusion metadata) still validates and the Open SWE 2/2 metric is unchanged. For scored sessions, require each finding source to be `development-calibration` (and reject other status mismatches) so excluded evidence cannot enter headline metrics.
findings.failureMode: Evidence explicitly marked excluded is nevertheless counted in development calibration results.
findings.title: Do not score findings from excluded source artifacts

findings.description: Existence alone does not establish a family's human disposition: `dispositionSourceArtifactId` can point at any review or panel artifact, including one explicitly classified as development evidence. Repointing PR 194's dismissed family from its operator disposition to the panel review is accepted and the metrics continue using that dismissal. Require the referenced artifact's calibration status to be `disposition-evidence` so scored labels cannot be backed by a non-disposition source.
findings.failureMode: A must-fix/non-blocking/dismissed label without designated disposition evidence is accepted and affects calibration metrics.
findings.title: Require an actual disposition-evidence source

findings.description: The live CLI compares only the three normalized argument strings and ignores both filesystem identity and the ledger's derived `.lock` path. A `--report` symlink/hard link to `--ledger` passes and the final report write truncates the completed ledger; even without links, choosing `--plan run.lock --ledger run` lets `Ledger.acquire` treat the plan as a stale lock and unlink it. Validate real/inode identities for all existing targets and include the derived ledger lock path before reading, running, or writing.
findings.failureMode: Lexically distinct artifact paths that alias each other or the ledger lock cause the run to destroy its plan or completed replay ledger.
findings.title: Validate every filesystem alias before the run

findings.description: Both modes run `cleanCloneRevision(root)`, while dry-run then writes the requested plan and live mode writes ledger/report files without requiring them to be outside the worktree or ignored. Thus the normal package-script sequence with relative `plan.json`, `ledger.jsonl`, and `report.json` succeeds only for dry-run: the live invocation sees its generated plan as an untracked dirty file and refuses; in-repo ledger/report artifacts likewise prevent the promised later replay. Make the cleanliness check ignore only the exact declared untracked artifacts while continuing to reject all tracked or unrelated changes.
findings.failureMode: Using ordinary relative artifact paths under the repository makes a generated plan unusable for live execution, or makes a successful ledger unusable for zero-call replay.
findings.title: Do not make generated artifacts poison the next CLI phase

findings.description: The source-identity denylist omits unique values that remain in every training input, including the finding title/description and `evidence.baseSha`, `evidence.headSha`, repository `revision`, and related hashes (the recursive omit list only removes differently named keys). A proposer can copy one of these training identifiers into either candidate string; the `proposal-invalid` check passes, child calls use the case-specific system prompt, and an otherwise eligible precision improvement can be selected despite the manifest's case-agnostic constraint. Remove identities from proposer feedback and reject every retained unique source value in the proposed pair.
findings.failureMode: A proposer response containing an exact training finding title, revision, or evidence hash is accepted as a general candidate and can produce an invalid case-specific experiment winner.
findings.title: Reject leaked source identities in proposed prompts

findings.description: The generated manifest promises that a runtime failure will “return no-improvement,” but `executeAdjudicationExperiment` records a failure row and rethrows, and the CLI therefore exits without writing a no-improvement report. A provider 429 or other listed divergence gives operators behavior opposite to the frozen plan. Since the implementation and tests deliberately fail loudly, change this manifest field to state that failures preserve evidence and abort rather than claiming a no-improvement return.
findings.failureMode: On a provider or execution failure, consumers following the run plan expect a no-improvement result/report but receive a rejected command with no report.
findings.title: Make the run-plan failure contract match execution

findings.description: The manifest hashes `packages/harnesses/src/index.ts` (and no factory-glue source/artifact), while live execution imports ignored `packages/harnesses/dist/index.js` and `packages/factory-glue/dist/index.js`. A Git-clean checkout can therefore execute stale generated JS; with the base harness build still present, this experiment omits `maxOutputTokens` but stale code reports a request bound of `undefined`, so `verifyTelemetry` aborts, while subtler drift can run behavior not represented by `codeHashes`. Rebuild from the frozen revision and hash/verify every imported dist artifact before opening credentials.
findings.failureMode: A live run from a Git-clean worktree with stale ignored harness output either fails the output-bound check or records results from code not bound by the manifest.
findings.title: Bind the generated artifacts the live run executes

findings.description: The corpus hashes raw `git diff` output but the command does not neutralize output-affecting Git configuration. On a supported developer host with `diff.noprefix=true`, for example, Git emits `--- path` instead of `--- a/path`; the bytes no longer match `selection.diff[1]`, so importing these newly registered golden tests fails with `Diff mismatch` even though the historical revisions are correct. Pass explicit canonical prefix/config options (and other output-affecting diff options) when materializing the frozen bytes.
findings.failureMode: A supported developer with a common global Git diff setting cannot run the golden suite or build the experiment plan because valid historical diffs fail their pinned hashes.
findings.title: Make frozen diff bytes independent of Git config

findings.description: The completed-ledger path recomputes and compares only `prior.result`, then returns `prior.report` verbatim. If a ledger's final result row has a modified report (for example altered call counts, served routes, or usage totals) while its result and operation rows remain valid, replay succeeds with zero calls and emits that false report. Recompute `report(ledger.rows, manifest, replayed)` and reject unless it matches the stored report before returning it.
findings.failureMode: A malformed or modified completed ledger produces a successful replay with an incorrect preserved report instead of being rejected as replay divergence.
findings.title: Verify the stored report during replay

findings.description: The retention gate builds `reported` from any decision carrying an expected blocker family ID, without requiring that decision to correspond to the blocker case. If the blocker row is downgraded while another row returns that family ID with `must-fix`, `acceptedBlockersRetained` remains true, so exact scores for otherwise-correct rows and all precision/retention objectives are not zeroed. Compute retention by matching each expected blocker to its decision at the same case/index (and validating its case/family) rather than searching family IDs globally.
findings.failureMode: A candidate downgrades an accepted blocker but emits its family ID as must-fix for a different case; the adapter reports retention 1 and leaves correct-row optimizer objectives nonzero despite the promised hard constraint.
findings.title: Bind blocker retention to the matching case

findings.description: Both replay lookups test the cached value's truthiness. A completed adjudication whose result is `null` (which the scorer explicitly supports as a contract failure) is stored in `ledger.cached`, but the next evaluation treats it as a miss and calls `adjudicate` again; the same occurs for a falsy proposal result. That breaks deterministic/selective replay and can duplicate model calls and ledger rows. Check `cached.has(key)` rather than the value at both lookup sites.
findings.failureMode: After an adjudicator returns null once, evaluating the same fixture/candidate again invokes the adjudicator instead of replaying the completed null result, permitting a different score and duplicate provider spend.
findings.title: Use key presence for replayed falsy results

findings.description: When a candidate gets any factual, causal, severity, disposition, or history field wrong without changing the reported must-fix families—for example, returning `refuted:dismissed` for `ordering-non-blocking`—`scores` contains a zero but every `scoreVectors` entry remains `{mustFixPrecision: 1, acceptedBlockerRetention: 1}`. AxGEPA prefers `scoreVectors` whenever present, so it ignores that zero and returns the incorrect instruction with a perfect Pareto score. Add a row/field classification-correctness dimension to the vectors Ax consumes.
findings.failureMode: An optimizer candidate misclassifies a non-blocking case while preserving blocker-family precision/retention; Ax receives perfect vectors and selects a wrong adjudication instruction.
findings.title: Include classification correctness in Ax vectors

findings.description: `acceptedBlockerRetention` is emitted as an ordinary Pareto dimension, so a seed candidate that changes `hunk-metadata-must-fix` to non-blocking remains a valid Ax result with `{mustFixPrecision: 1, acceptedBlockerRetention: 0}` when no retained-blocker candidate dominates it. This returns a blocker-dropping instruction despite the promised hard constraint. Treat retention failure as infeasible and refuse any Ax result whose retention is zero rather than exposing it as a tradeable objective.
findings.failureMode: The seed/proposed instruction omits an accepted must-fix case and no candidate dominates it; Ax returns a blocker-dropping instruction despite the promised hard retention constraint.
findings.title: Make blocker retention an actual hard constraint

findings.description: The aggregate sets trust `familyId` from every decision without first matching `caseId` to a known case. If the hunk blocker is returned under a mistyped case ID, its real row is `missing` and the typo row is `unknown`, yet retention remains 1 because the unknown output claimed the expected family. Derive accepted/retained families only from valid decisions matched to their known case and expected family; an unknown must-fix may remain a false positive, but it must not count as retaining the blocker.
findings.failureMode: The must-fix decision's case ID is mistyped or attached to another case while retaining the expected family ID; scoring says the accepted blocker was retained although its actual case is missing.
findings.title: Exclude unknown cases from blocker retention
