findings.description: The fixture declares `context.input.baseSha` as its runtime-provenance field and copies that value into every `executingRuntimeSha`. However, the panel input producer sets `baseSha` to GitHub's `merge_base_commit.sha`, which identifies the reviewed diff's base, not the revision of the deployed factory-host process. When main/deployment advances while a PR remains based on an older commit, this evaluator reports the old merge base as the executing runtime and falsely satisfies the runtime-provenance metric. Capture a build/runtime SHA independently in each snapshot and derive these values from that field.
findings.failureMode: For a panel run served by deployment B against a PR whose merge base is A, the continuity output reports A in `executingRuntimeShas`, producing incorrect AC-7 provenance.
findings.title: Runtime provenance is sourced from the PR merge base

findings.description: `assertFixture` validates fields inside each run but never enforces unique `snapshotRunId` (or another run identity). A malformed continuity fixture that repeats one stored panel row passes validation; `computeContinuityMetrics` then counts the same run twice, inflating authoritative/pending run totals, adjudication appearances, repeat rates, and calibration. Track source run IDs while validating and reject duplicates before aggregation.
findings.failureMode: Passing a fixture with the same `snapshotRunId` twice causes one stored run to be reported as two and changes all appearance-based continuity metrics.
findings.title: Reject duplicate panel source runs

findings.description: The Open SWE validator checks only that `family` is nonempty and does not require unique thread IDs. Repeating one thread record therefore passes validation and `threads: fixture.openSweThreads.length` reports two threads for the same review finding, while `uniqueFamilies` stays unchanged. Track `thread.id` values and reject duplicates before computing the comparison.
findings.failureMode: A fixture containing the same Open SWE thread record twice reports an inflated thread count and a false session-wide comparison.
findings.title: Reject duplicate Open SWE threads

findings.description: The evaluator collapses an explicitly blank `PANEL_JUDGE_NATIVE_MODEL` into the Sol default, but only supplies that default when native is the primary. Thus a blank native-primary configuration runs Sol here even though `factory-host/src/index.ts` rejects it, while an unset native fallback is left model-less and fails if the subscription primary goes down even though the server defaults that fallback to Sol. Derive the model whenever either route is native, distinguish unset from set-but-blank, and reject the latter so golden/fidelity runs exercise the same route as production.
findings.failureMode: With `PANEL_JUDGE_HARNESS=native` and an explicitly empty native-model variable, golden evaluation silently runs the default rather than rejecting production-invalid config; with `PANEL_JUDGE_HARNESS=claude`, `PANEL_JUDGE_FALLBACK_HARNESS=native`, no model variable, and a Claude failure, the evaluator cannot invoke the production-valid Sol fallback and records a failed run.
findings.title: Match native-model defaulting to the server

findings.description: On `CredentialDataError` this branch throws but leaves the prior snapshot intact (the new test even asserts that retention). If a row is replaced by plaintext, corrupt ciphertext, or an envelope under an unknown key, one call rejects, but a subsequent database outage enters the generic degraded branch and serves the old cached API/OAuth token. Thus a credential already known to be untrustworthy or superseded can be used again, defeating the stated fail-closed boundary and potentially continuing access with a revoked credential. Delete/poison that provider's snapshot on any data-integrity error (and on the analogous failing `load`) so degraded mode cannot revive it until a successful validated read.
findings.failureMode: After observing an invalid encrypted row, a later DB outage revives and uses the previously cached credential instead of failing closed.
findings.title: Poison the snapshot after credential-integrity failures

findings.description: This return enters the locked refresh/rewrite without first invalidating the existing snapshot; the base code used to replace the snapshot with the just-read row before refreshing. If a cached still-live credential A has since been replaced in the database by expired credential B, and refreshing/writing B fails, the old A remains cached. On a later DB outage the degraded branch serves A again, so replacement/revocation is bypassed. Keep the commit-before-publish rule for the new credential, but mark the old snapshot unusable as soon as a validated live read shows that locked work is required, restoring it only after a successful current read/commit.
findings.failureMode: A failed refresh or rotation leaves a superseded cached token eligible for degraded use, allowing later requests to authenticate with the old credential.
findings.title: Invalidate superseded snapshots before refresh work

findings.description: The `57014`/`55P03` catch wraps the whole transaction, including the newly added re-encryption UPDATE loop and COMMIT, not just `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`. If a shadowed previous-key row's UPDATE is cancelled with SQLSTATE 57014 after the lock was acquired, this branch rolls back and then immediately serves the valid selected current-key row as if lock contention were harmless. The caller sees success although the old-key row was not rewritten; retiring that previous key then makes every read fail closed on the still-shadowed row. Restrict timeout recovery to the lock query and propagate refresh/write/commit failures.
findings.failureMode: A post-lock re-encryption write timeout is silently treated as lock contention, leaving an old-key row behind and causing credential outage when that key is retired.
findings.title: Recover only when the lock acquisition timed out

findings.description: If the unlocked read sees an API-key row that needs key rotation, `getApiKey` calls `refreshLocked(provider)` without an OAuth provider. A concurrent Factory login can replace that row with a valid OAuth credential before the lock is acquired; the locked path then commits and snapshots the OAuth row but returns `undefined` through `oauth?.getApiKey(next)` (and the timeout-recovery branch has the same issue), so an otherwise valid native request fails. Resolve `getOAuthProvider(provider)` from the locked/fresh credential type instead of carrying the pre-lock type decision.
findings.failureMode: Concurrent API-key-to-OAuth replacement during a rotation lock causes `getApiKey` to return undefined for a valid credential.
findings.title: Resolve the OAuth provider after locking

findings.description: This feature PR changes the deployed host from code-sdk 1.1.2/core 1.56.0/Factory 0.4.0/pg 1.19.0/Mastra 1.23.0 to a new release cohort (with matching bumps in the other manifests and lockfile). The base repository mandate requires every upstream bump to be its own contract-tested PR; the bootstrap exception does not apply because `contract-tests/` already exists at base and the appendix records no explicit bootstrap adjudication. Merging this as-is bypasses the repository's dependency-release gate and ships all upstream behavior changes together with the credential feature; move the cohort alignment to its own version-bump PR.
findings.failureMode: A feature merge directly deploys multiple upstream runtime upgrades without the mandatory isolated dependency-upgrade gate.
findings.title: Split upstream bumps out of the feature PR

findings.description: On the default `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` native judge path, OpenAI's `response.created` event supplies the actual model and AI SDK carries that provider value in `result.response.modelId`. This condition drops it solely because its bare value equals the request, so a normal successful adjudication exposes `modelReported: null` and `runEnsemble` propagates the wrong identity. The bare-model Claude SDK wrapper is the path that fabricates `response.modelId` from configuration; distinguish that path (for example, trust `response.modelId` for namespaced native requests) instead of discarding equal native response metadata.
findings.failureMode: A normal successful default native OpenAI adjudication where the provider reports `gpt-5.6-sol` records null rather than the provider-reported model, corrupting decision provenance and the ensemble's `judgeModelReported`.
findings.title: Keep native OpenAI's reported model when it matches the request

findings.description: The fixture declares `context.input.baseSha` as the source of every `executingRuntimeSha`, but ingestion explicitly fills that field from GitHub's `merge_base_commit`, and the panel prompt itself describes it as the repository base revision. Thus the default reports `cfaf…`—and the post-deploy rows report preceding merge bases—as deployed runtime revisions without any recorded runtime/build identity. If deployment is lagging, ahead, or rebuilt from another revision, AC-7 and the emitted runtime-provenance result are false. Capture an actual runtime revision or label these values as merge-base SHAs.
findings.failureMode: Whenever the deployed panel revision differs from a PR's merge base, the frozen evaluator reports the merge-base commit as the executing runtime and falsely claims shared runtime provenance.
findings.title: Do not treat the PR merge base as runtime provenance

findings.description: The new continuity scorer uses `Math.round`, while both existing golden scorers deliberately round exact half-tenths to even. A valid continuity fixture whose rate lands on a half-tenth (for example 1/16 = 6.25%) is emitted as 6.3% instead of the golden-eval convention's 6.2%, so the standalone and integrated metric output disagrees with the repository's scoring convention. Reuse the half-even calculation.
findings.failureMode: For a valid fixture with a one-in-sixteen percentage, the CLI emits 6.3% rather than the golden scorers' half-even 6.2%.
findings.title: Use the established half-even metric rounding

findings.description: On the default native OpenAI judge path, the AI SDK sets `response.modelId` from the provider's `response.created.response.model`, which normally equals the requested model. This condition records it only when it differs, so a successful `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` decision is emitted with `modelReported: null` and the ensemble loses the provider identity this change is meant to preserve. Trust `response.modelId` for native AI-SDK calls while keeping the configured-only Claude SDK value excluded via caller-specific handling.
findings.failureMode: A normal native OpenAI decision returns provider model `gpt-5.6-sol`, equal to configured `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`; `decisionGenerationMetadata` drops it and downstream `judgeModelReported` is null despite provider evidence.
findings.title: Preserve matching native OpenAI model identities

findings.description: Both the `adjudicate` call here and the `propose` call on line 19 let exceptions escape without first recording a fatal exit. The pinned Ax implementation swallows adapter exceptions, and ADR-007 therefore requires adapters on this boundary to own the abort. Replacing the test proposer with one that always throws still returns `bestScore: 1`, a Pareto result, and exit code 0, so the new golden certification can pass even though the proposer path is broken; a throwing adjudicator similarly falls through to `program.forward` and returns normally. Wrap both entry points in an exit-3/fatal boundary before rethrowing.
findings.failureMode: An adjudicator, proposer, scoring, or ledger exception is swallowed by Ax, allowing the evaluation or its tests to exit successfully with an incomplete or bogus optimization result.
findings.title: Convert swallowed adapter errors into fatal exits

findings.description: The distinct-path guard compares only the three literal paths and ignores the lock file derived as `${ledgerPath}.lock`. With `--plan /tmp/run.lock --ledger /tmp/run`, the plan is read successfully, then `Ledger.open` treats that JSON plan as a stale lock and unlinks it before executing; an existing report at that derived lock path is deleted the same way. Symlink or hard-link aliases can likewise make the final report write truncate the completed ledger. Canonicalize targets and parents and include the derived lock path/same-inode checks before opening anything.
findings.failureMode: A plan or report path equal to the derived ledger lock path is deleted during startup, and filesystem aliases can make the final report write destroy the ledger.
findings.title: Reject collisions with the ledger lock path

findings.description: The `finally` block awaits `calls.close()` before `ledger.close()` without a nested `finally`. If the credential store's asynchronous pool shutdown rejects, execution skips the ledger close, leaves `<ledger>.lock` owned by the still-live process, and converts an otherwise completed run into an exception; a subsequent library invocation in that process is then refused as `ledger lock held by live pid`. Put `ledger.close()` in an inner `finally` so lock release cannot be bypassed by harness cleanup.
findings.failureMode: A database-pool close rejection strands the ledger lock and crashes a completed run; retries in the same process remain blocked.
findings.title: Always release the ledger lock when harness close fails

findings.description: `omitIdentity` only removes a small set of key names before forwarding the full training input. The forwarded object still contains `context.title`, `evidence.baseSha/headSha`, each repository blob's `path` and `revision`, and file names embedded in `diff`; the later blacklist covers only the finding file and selected diff path. A proposer can therefore copy or branch on an evidence path/hash (for example `evals/golden/corpus-split.mjs`) and the result can pass `proposal-invalid`, global eligibility, and held-out precision as a supposedly case-agnostic winner. Build a positive, identity-free feedback projection (or comprehensively reject every source identifier) before invoking the proposer.
findings.failureMode: A model proposal containing a training-only evidence path or revision is accepted and can produce a falsely promotable, source-specific experiment winner.
findings.title: Remove all source identities from proposer feedback

findings.description: Completed replay compares the recomputed selection only with `prior.result` and then returns `prior.report` verbatim. If the result row's report (or terminal usage/model/wall-time fields plus that report) is edited while decision outputs remain intact, `verifyReplayInventory` and the Ax replay both pass and the CLI republishes fabricated telemetry/metrics as a successful zero-call replay. Recompute `report(ledger.rows, manifest, replayed)`, validate the terminal metadata against the manifest/intents, and reject any difference from the stored report before returning it.
findings.failureMode: A corrupted or edited completed ledger replays successfully and emits a false preserved experiment report.
findings.title: Recompute the report during ledger replay

findings.description: The live CLI never checks that its three paths identify distinct files before this `writeFile`. If `--report` aliases `--ledger`, a successful run closes and then truncates the immutable ledger into the summary report; if it aliases `--plan`, it destroys the registered plan. Canonicalize paths and compare existing targets by device/inode, refusing collisions before any open or write.
findings.failureMode: A valid live invocation using the same pathname, symlink, or hardlink for report and ledger/plan succeeds through provider execution and then irreversibly overwrites an audit artifact.
findings.title: Reject aliased plan, ledger, and report paths

findings.description: The incompleteness check only detects an intent with no terminal. A process interruption after `model-call-terminal` is synced but before the adapter row is appended therefore passes this guard; executing that exact ledger shape repeated all five planned calls and reported six successful calls because the orphaned terminal was counted too. Refuse any non-final ledger whose intent/terminal/adapter sequence is not complete and exact.
findings.failureMode: Killing the process in the append gap after the first successful terminal and retrying the ledger repeats that paid operation and reports six successful calls for a five-operation plan.
findings.title: Treat terminal-without-adapter rows as incomplete

findings.description: When a ledger contains `micro-pilot-result`, this immediately runs Ax against whatever replay rows remain and only checks `calls.cursor` afterward. If the first adjudication cache row is missing while the result row survives, the adapter treats it as a cache miss and makes a new paid provider request; an executed damaged-ledger replay made one call before raising `replay-divergence`. Preflight the exact expected cache inventory before constructing/running Ax.
findings.failureMode: Replaying a completed ledger whose first adjudication row is damaged causes an unexpected live model call and spend instead of refusing without loading credentials.
findings.title: Validate the first replay row before compiling

findings.description: The failed/incomplete-ledger guard throws inside this `try`, but this catch appends another `micro-pilot-failure` whenever the existing ledger has rows. Thus merely retrying a preserved failed ledger changes its bytes and invalidates the hash-bound evidence/report instead of refusing it unchanged. Do not append a new failure when rejection happened before this invocation added any row.
findings.failureMode: Running the CLI again against either committed failed ledger appends a duplicate failure record, so its SHA-256 no longer matches `failure-report.json`.
findings.title: Keep rejected failed ledgers byte-preserving

findings.description: Completed replay validates only the Ax `result`; it returns `prior.report` verbatim without checking it against the ledger's terminal rows. In execution, changing only `report.totalTokens` to 999999 still produced `replay: true` with zero calls and emitted that false total. Recompute `report(ledger.rows)` and require it to match the preserved report before returning.
findings.failureMode: A completed ledger whose summary report is corrupted but whose cached decisions and Ax result remain intact replays successfully and writes the corrupted report as authoritative output.
findings.title: Recompute the replay report from terminal rows

findings.description: The live branch derives only `git rev-parse HEAD`, and the dry-run branch at line 107 also constructs a revision-tagged plan without the existing pilot's `git status --porcelain` check. With uncommitted edits to the runner or native-harness path that do not alter plan reconstruction, generated plans and live ledgers are attributed to the unchanged commit even though different code produced them or made the calls. Run one clean-clone preflight before either branch.
findings.failureMode: On a developer host with an edited `native-harness.mjs`, the live CLI records the clean commit SHA as the execution revision although uncommitted code makes the provider calls; dry-run similarly emits a falsely attributed plan.
findings.title: Refuse dirty source before revision attribution

findings.description: Live execution imports the ignored `packages/harnesses/dist` and `packages/factory-glue/dist` builds, while the plan records no hash for either. After building one commit and checking out another, `git status` can be clean while this line loads previous-commit harness or credential-store code, so calls are falsely attributed to the new plan revision. Rebuild/verify these modules from current source or bind their bytes into the registered plan before calling them.
findings.failureMode: A developer builds commit A, checks out commit B without rebuilding, and runs B's plan; the ledger claims revision B while commit A's ignored harness/glue code serves the live run.
findings.title: Bind ignored build artifacts to the recorded revision

findings.description: These evals now use org-first resolution, but all three native harness routes require OAuth and reject API-key snapshots. With a normal org-scoped API key plus a fallback user's valid OAuth login, the store selects the org key and the lane/judge fails (`Not logged in to xAI` in a direct reproduction) without making a provider request. Apply OAuth-compatible selection to `lane.mjs:135`, `ensemble.mjs:59`, `match.mjs:111`, and `optimize/pilot.mjs:38` while retaining the intended scope policy.
findings.failureMode: Golden lane, ensemble judge, matcher judge, and optimizer fail whenever an org API key shadows the fallback user's valid OAuth credential.
findings.title: Do not select org API keys for OAuth-only native evals

findings.description: When an old-key API-key row triggers this call, another writer can replace the row with a valid OAuth credential between the initial read and the locked re-read. `refreshLocked` then receives no provider, commits/snapshots the OAuth row, and returns `undefined` via `oauth?.getApiKey(next)`, so a usable credential is reported missing. Pass or resolve the provider for the locked row rather than relying on the pre-lock credential type.
findings.failureMode: Concurrent API-key-to-OAuth replacement during key rotation produces an undefined credential despite a valid locked OAuth row.
findings.title: Resolve the OAuth provider again after locking

findings.description: This feature PR changes the runtime `@mastra/factory` pin (and the coupled code-sdk/core/pg/mastra pins), although the base hard rule requires upstream version bumps to be their own PR. The bootstrap exception is unavailable here because the Factory/provider contract-test gate already existed at the base revision. Split the cohort adoption into the mandated dependency PR before landing the credential feature.
findings.failureMode: The feature merge bypasses the mandatory standalone dependency-upgrade release rail for the new runtime cohort.
findings.title: Move the cohort bump to its required standalone PR

findings.description: This condition discards `response.modelId` whenever its bare value equals the request. That is needed for `ClaudeSDKAgent`, whose wrapper synthesizes the configured ID, but it is wrong for native AI SDK providers, where `response.modelId` is the model returned by the provider stream. A normal native OpenAI decision whose `response.created` reports `gpt-5.6-sol` therefore emits `modelReported: null` (reproduced against the pinned provider), so the new evaluator provenance loses the serving identity on the default judge path. Pass the evidence source/provider into this helper and suppress only the Claude wrapper's synthetic field, while retaining native response IDs.
findings.failureMode: The default native OpenAI judge returns the exact requested model ID and the evaluator envelope incorrectly reports that provider identity as unknown.
findings.title: Preserve exact-match native model reports

findings.description: The new completeness check equates every non-null lane usage object with valid usage. `runLane`'s existing normalizer returns an all-zero object for any non-empty but unrecognized provider shape (for example `{ billable_tokens: 12 }`), so a successful set of lanes with such a response is now published as `usage.complete: true` even though its token usage was not captured. Validate that each lane usage contains recognized, safe counters (or make normalization return null for unrecognized shapes) before setting completeness.
findings.failureMode: A provider returns a non-empty usage payload using unknown fields, and the ensemble falsely certifies its aggregate token usage as complete.
findings.title: Do not treat unrecognized lane usage as complete

findings.description: Returning at the first invalid value preserves only a prefix, not all known usage. If an untrusted lane/provider emits a malformed token total (for example a fractional value) and a later lane reports 10 valid tokens, the ensemble records 0 known tokens and `complete: false`, discarding the later known charge; the same helper also undercounts later baseline runs. Keep `complete = false` but continue scanning and add every subsequent safe value that still fits.
findings.failureMode: One malformed usage total precedes valid lane or run totals, causing evaluator output to discard all later known token usage.
findings.title: Continue past an invalid usage entry

findings.description: On the default native OpenAI route, a successful provider response that reports exactly `gpt-5.6-sol` is discarded solely because it equals the configured model. The pinned Agent exposes the `response.created` model as `response.modelId` and marks the result with OpenAI provider metadata, yet the ensemble consequently records `judgeModelReported: null`. Distinguish this native provider response from the Claude SDK's configured echo instead of using value inequality as the evidence test.
findings.failureMode: A successful default openai/gpt-5.6-sol judge call reports model gpt-5.6-sol; generation provenance and the ensemble nevertheless emit modelReported null.
findings.title: Native OpenAI drops a reported matching model

findings.description: Native decision calls (and the three changed Claude decision calls at lines 736, 742, and 748) leave structured output in strict mode, so the pinned Agent/Claude SDK throws before returning its completed result. On malformed model JSON—the path that triggers repair—the new `DecisionCallError` therefore records null model/usage even when the provider response contained both: an invalid-then-valid xAI run consumed 15 tokens twice but reports only the repair's 15-token lower bound. Use the supported non-throwing `errorStrategy: 'warn'` and perform the existing local parse afterward so the catch can attach returned metadata.
findings.failureMode: A native or Claude judge returns malformed/schema-invalid JSON with provider model and token usage, then repair succeeds; provenance marks the first generation's reported model and usage unknown and undercounts known cost.
findings.title: Schema repairs discard known generation metadata

findings.description: `validateFamily` only checks that `dispositionSourceArtifactId` names an artifact, while `operator-disposition` artifacts are self-hashed but never projected against the frozen issue-comment response. An edited corpus can rewrite a disposition comment, relabel an accepted family as dismissed, recompute the artifact hash, and still validate; the resulting precision is then based on fabricated ground truth. Bind operator dispositions to the matching raw issue-comment ID/content/author and reject inappropriate disposition-source kinds.
findings.failureMode: Given a corpus whose accepted family is relabeled dismissed and whose operator artifact is rewritten/rehashed without changing the raw issue-comment bytes, validation succeeds and precision falls from 60% to 40%.
findings.title: Bind disposition evidence to frozen comments

findings.description: Validation walks whichever sessions are present but never proves that each development-calibration review/panel artifact belongs to exactly one calibrated session or that each development-calibration family appears in a calibrated finding. Deleting a session therefore leaves its frozen source artifacts and family labels intact, passes validation, and silently removes that system's true/false positives from every metric. Reconcile session membership against the complete calibrated artifact and family inventories and reject omissions or reuse.
findings.failureMode: Deleting the PR 196 Open SWE session from an otherwise unchanged loaded corpus leaves its calibrated family and source artifacts present, but validation succeeds and precision changes from 60% (3/5) to 50% (2/4).
findings.title: Reject orphaned calibrated evidence

findings.description: The Open SWE branch accepts any included review comment containing `🟡`; it never checks the source author, the `open-swe-review-comment` marker, that it is a root comment, or that `source.reviewId` equals the session's `reviewId`. An operator reply or unrelated review comment containing that emoji can therefore be labeled as an Open SWE finding and counted as a blocking medium report under the wrong session/head. Require the frozen source to be an Open SWE root finding belonging to this review session (including author/marker and review ID checks).
findings.failureMode: Given a review thread where a non-bot reply contains or quotes the yellow-dot token, a corpus can select that reply as `sourceArtifactId`; validation succeeds and precision/phase metrics count it as an Open SWE finding even though Open SWE did not report it in that session.
findings.title: Authenticate Open SWE finding comments instead of matching an emoji

findings.description: The metric named and advertised as `severityDispositionErrors` compares only the finding's blocking bit with the family's delivery disposition; it never compares `finding.reportedSeverity` with `family.consequenceSeverity`. A proven must-fix reported at the wrong severity but still marked blocking is therefore reported as having no severity/disposition error. Count a family when either its reported/consequence severity or its blocking/disposition classification disagrees.
findings.failureMode: For an otherwise valid calibrated family whose finding is reported `medium`, adjudicated consequence is `high`, and both sides classify it as blocking/must-fix, validation succeeds but `severityDispositionErrors` remains zero instead of identifying the severity error.
findings.title: Include severity mismatches in severity/disposition errors

findings.description: The record validator verifies only that `record.source` SHAs look like SHAs; it never parses the `github:<n>:pull` raw source or checks its PR number, repository, base/head/merge SHAs, and merge time against the record. A corpus can therefore relabel valid review data as a different PR/source commit and still validate, so the supposedly exact frozen interval can carry false provenance. Parse the required pull raw source and compare its identity/provenance fields to `record.pullRequest` and `record.source`.
findings.failureMode: Given a record whose source head/base/merge SHA or PR URL is replaced with another syntactically valid value while all frozen raw bytes stay unchanged, `validateAdjudicationCorpus` succeeds and exposes a corpus with incorrect source provenance.
findings.title: Cross-check record provenance against the raw pull response

findings.description: `computeAdjudicationMetrics` validates the corpus and derives every current metric, but returns `corpus.legacy.metrics` verbatim; `validateAdjudicationCorpus` does not inspect `legacy` at all. A caller that clones, deserializes, or mutates the loaded corpus can therefore supply arbitrary legacy regression numbers that are reported as validated even while the hashed `legacy.fixture` is unchanged. Derive this field with `computeContinuityMetrics(corpus.legacy.fixture)` (or validate exact equality) inside the computation.
findings.failureMode: Starting from `loadAdjudicationCorpus()`, replacing only `corpus.legacy.metrics.panel.blockingCalibration` with fabricated values still passes the validation performed by `computeAdjudicationMetrics` and emits those values in `legacyRegressionOnly`.
findings.title: Recompute legacy metrics instead of trusting a cached field

findings.description: When the deployed Factory 0.10 host enables its new `secretEncryption` option, it migrates `model_provider_credentials.data` from an `AuthCredential` object to a `mastra:factory-secret:v1:` string. The still-active `FactoryCredentialStore` selects and casts that raw column directly; native-reviewer boot preflight then sees `cred.type !== 'oauth'` and aborts startup, and live reads cannot refresh/use the token either. The cohort bump needs to pass the matching Factory decrypter/key configuration into this adapter (or read through Factory's credential domain) before claiming compatibility with the 0.10 credential table.
findings.failureMode: Start factory-host with an enabled native reviewer against a Factory 0.10 database whose credentials were encrypted by Factory; startup throws `native reviewer preflight failed`, making the panel unavailable.
findings.title: Factory 0.10 encrypted credentials cannot be read

findings.description: The appendix now declares the pilot pinned to the Factory 0.10 cohort, but the repository's indexed, operator-apply `docs/mastra-7-factory-host-wiring.patch` still stages Factory 0.4, Core 1.56-era resolutions, and an old factory-glue commit, and patches the old 0.4.0 package. An operator following the documented deployment path therefore does not deploy the cohort this PR validates (or may fail to apply the old anchors). Regenerate that operator artifact for the 0.10/1.62 cohort and the current glue revision as part of this pin change.
findings.failureMode: Apply the canonical factory-host wiring artifact after merging this PR; the external Factory host remains on Factory 0.4/Core 1.56 and old factory-glue instead of the adopted cohort, so production behavior diverges from all updated contract tests.
findings.title: Deployment artifact still installs the old cohort

findings.description: The default native OpenAI judge receives its served identity from the required `response.created.response.model` field, which the AI SDK exposes as `response.modelId`; when that identity equals the requested model (the normal `gpt-5.6-sol` case), this condition deliberately drops it. A successful default adjudication therefore records `generation.modelReported` and `judgeModelReported` as null despite provider evidence. Preserve this trustworthy native OpenAI response identity even when it equals the configured request, while continuing to reject configuration-only values from lanes such as the Claude SDK wrapper.
findings.failureMode: A successful mainline native OpenAI adjudication returns null model provenance despite the provider response carrying the served model, so evaluator records lose the identity this change is intended to preserve.
findings.title: Exact OpenAI model IDs are discarded

findings.description: Individual provider counts are bounded with `Number.isSafeInteger`, but these cross-attempt additions do not verify that cumulative values stay safe. Two locally complete attempts with totals `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` and `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER - 1` are reported as the exact `complete` total `18014398509481980` instead of `18014398509481981`. This can reach the production wrapper when an untrusted provider returns a schema-valid but coverage-invalid first decision (triggering repair) and then a valid repair; use checked arithmetic and mark the aggregate incomplete when any sum leaves the safe-integer range.
findings.failureMode: Two recorded provider attempts with individually valid usage can overflow JavaScript's exact-integer range and produce an incorrect evaluator usage total labeled complete.
findings.title: Attempt usage sums can round while marked complete
